critic.fix_suggestion: Divide the fuselage and wing primitive faces into three distinct material zones to replicate the tri-color scheme. Assign a white material to the upper 40% of the fuselage, a purple material to the lower 60%, and a secondary gold/yellow accent strip at the 40% boundary line. For the vertical stabilizer, apply a purple base material and place a small, gold-colored rectangular prism (scaled to 5% of the tail's surface area) centered on the upper half to represent the logo.

discrepancies.observed: Solid uniform gray color across the entire fuselage and wings.
discrepancies.reference: White upper fuselage with purple underbelly and tail accents.
discrepancies.direction_of_fix: Apply multi-color material segments to different primitive faces.

discrepancies.observed: Plain gray vertical stabilizer without any markings.
discrepancies.reference: Gold Thai Airways logo on a purple vertical stabilizer.
discrepancies.direction_of_fix: Add a smaller, colored geometric shape or decal to the tail surface.

discrepancies.reference: Light gray/white engines with specific color banding.
discrepancies.direction_of_fix: Change material colors of the cylinder primitives representing the engines.

discrepancies.observed: No text or logos on the side of the aircraft.
discrepancies.reference: Prominent 'THAI' lettering and gold stripes along the fuselage.
discrepancies.direction_of_fix: Add thin, elongated rectangular prisms to represent the livery stripes.
